title: KV cache lifecycle hardening and observability overhaul
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a capacity storm on 2026-02-08 a combination of an async compaction race and an eviction-score drift caused persistent slab fragmentation and a per-instance memory increase that ultimately led to OOM on several Dedicated hosts. Root cause analysis shows: (1) a race between compaction and concurrent insert/evict paths that left partially-updated slab metadata, (2) eviction score decay logic that allowed low-priority entries to starve better eviction candidates, and (3) insufficient telemetry to surface multi-tenant prefix namespace pressure early. The incident caused throughput degradation and 3 hours of degraded availability for affected customers.

This ticket tracks the follow-up work: immediate mitigations, medium-term fixes, new telemetry/alerts, test harnesses, and rollout/rollback plans. It prioritizes changes that unblock customers quickly while preserving options for a more invasive refactor if the fixes are insufficient.
action_items: Hotfix: backport PR to force synchronous slab metadata flush on compaction path (owner: Marcus Liu, ETA: 2026-02-18) - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4721
Add pre- and post-compaction checksums + compact operation log for forensic replay (owner: Priya Nair, ETA: 2026-03-01)

Eviction algorithm emergency tweak: add minimum decay floor parameter to prevent starvation under bursty insert patterns; expose as runtime flag with default on for Dedicated (owner: Ethan Park, ETA: 2026-02-25)

Dashboard and alerts: new Grafana panel 'kv_prefixcache/namespace_pressure' and alert 'KCACHE_NAMESPACE_PRESSURE_HIGH' (threshold: 75th percentile slab occupancy + eviction latency > 500ms sustained for 5m) (owner: Sofia Romero, ETA: 2026-02-20)
Create a synthetic chaos test in CI that simulates concurrent compaction+evict+insert with tenant skew and verify invariants (owner: Marcus Liu, ETA: 2026-03-08)
Develop an offline diagnostic tool to scan slab files for tombstone / header inconsistencies and produce repair scripts (owner: Daniel Kim, ETA: 2026-03-10)

Run a canary on dedicated-staging with the hotfix and telemetry enabled for 72 hours before broader rollout; collect memory growth, eviction churn, and tail-latency traces (owner: Marcus Liu, ETA: 2026-03-12)

Post-deploy: run a targeted audit of all active Dedicated customers to identify ones with historically high namespace skew and proactively schedule capacity adjustments (owner: Customer Success, ETA: 2026-03-20)
Long-term: spec a slab allocator refactor to reduce fragmentation risk and allow background compaction scheduling with global coordination (owner: Research/Applied ML + Runtime, ETA: Q3 2026)
Document incident lessons and update runbooks: add 'kv-cache memory growth triage' steps including quick rollback and emergency tombstone-sweep command snippets (owner: Sofia Romero, ETA: 2026-02-22)
comments: 2026-02-10 Marcus Liu: Initial triage complete. Reproduced memory growth locally with the provided tenant replay. Found compaction left a 'header_count' mismatch between in-memory map and on-disk slab index.

2026-02-12 Priya Nair: Reviewed compaction hotfix PR. Concern about synchronous flush adding tail latency under normal load. Proposal: gate sync flush behind a runtime flag and enable only during emergency rollout.
2026-02-14 Sofia Romero: Dashboard prototype uploaded to grafana/dashboards/kv_prefixcache.json. Need feedback on useful percentiles and namespace tagging.
2026-02-18 Marcus Liu: Hotfix PR merged into release-1.22 branch and cherry-picked to hotfix-1.21. Deployed to dedicated-staging; initial memory growth halted in canary hosts.
2026-02-21 Ethan Park: Eviction floor feature implemented and tested. Bench results: negligible impact on steady-state tail latency, reduces eviction churn by ~22% under synthetic burst.
2026-02-24 Daniel Kim: Diagnostic scanner v0.1 ready. Found 4 slab files with inconsistent tombstone counts in the incident window. Will bake repair steps into a non-destructive dry-run mode.
2026-02-26 Marcus Liu: Canary completed (72h). Memory growth stable; no regression in p99 latency. Preparing rollout notes and rollback plan.
